{"code": "## Step 1: Deduplicate on patient_id, keeping highest sample_seq
# This ensures one row per patient

# Sort by patient_id and sample_seq (descending) to prioritize higher sample_seq
df_dedup = df.sort_values(by=['patient_id', 'sample_seq'], ascending=[True, False]).drop_duplicates(subset=['patient_id'], keep='first')

print(f"After deduplication: {len(df_dedup)} unique patients")
print(f"Patient_id uniqueness after dedup: {df_dedup['patient_id'].nunique()}")

# Check that we now have one row per patient
assert len(df_dedup) == df_dedup['patient_id'].nunique(), "Deduplication failed - multiple rows per patient"

# Now check the severity distribution
severe_count = df_dedup['severity'].eq('severe').sum()
total_patients = len(df_dedup)
fraction_severe = severe_count / total_patients

print(f"Number of patients with severe baseline disease: {severe_count}")
print(f"Total number of patients: {total_patients}")
print(f"Fraction with severe baseline disease: {fraction_severe}")"}
